chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
So that the full measurement is not achieved until it tilts (in favor of the buyer).
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a measurement to be 'complete' in Islamic trade ethics?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'tarjih' (tilting the scale) as a recommended act of generosity (mustahabb) to ensure the buyer receives a slight surplus, thereby fulfilling the spirit of fair trade. This practice reflects the ethical emphasis on benevolence in commercial transactions, distinguishing between strict legal equality and moral perfection. It underscores the Imam's teaching that true fulfillment involves going beyond the minimum requirement to benefit the other party.
